Combine Multiple Imputation Estimates and Sampling Covariance Matrix

Source: R/miHelper-mi-combine.R
MICombine.Rd

Combine Multiple Imputation Estimates and Sampling Covariance Matrix

Usage

MICombine(object, adj = FALSE)

Arguments

object

Object of class mifit, that is, the output of the MIFit() function.

adj

Logical. If adj = TRUE, use Li, Raghunathan, and Rubin (1991) adjustment.

Value

Returns a list with the following elements:

M

Number of imputations \(M\).

est

Vector of pooled coefficients/parameter estimates \(\bar{\boldsymbol{\theta}}\).

within

Covariance within imputations \(\boldsymbol{V}_{\mathrm{within}}\).

between

Covariance between imputations \(\boldsymbol{V}_{\mathrm{between}}\).

total

Total covariance matrix \(\boldsymbol{V}_{\mathrm{total}}\).

ariv

Average relative increase in variance (NA if adj = FALSE).

total_adj

Adjusted total covariance matrix \(\tilde{\boldsymbol{V}}_{\mathrm{total}}\) (NA if adj = FALSE).

Details

The pooled vector of parameter estimates is given by $$ \bar{\boldsymbol{\theta}} = M^{-1} \sum_{m = 1}^{M} \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{m} $$ where \(M\) is the number of imputations, \(m = \left\{ 1, 2, \cdots, M \right\}\), and \(\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{m}\) is the vector of parameter estimates for the \(m^{\mathrm{th}}\) imputation.

The pooled or total sampling variance-covariance matrix consists of combining between and within imputation variances given by $$ \boldsymbol{V}_{\mathrm{within}} = M^{-1} \sum_{m = 1}^{M} \operatorname{Var} \left( \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{m} \right) $$

$$ \boldsymbol{V}_{\mathrm{between}} = \left( M - 1 \right)^{-1} \sum_{m = 1}^{M} \left( \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{m} - \bar{\boldsymbol{\theta}} \right) \left( \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{m} - \bar{\boldsymbol{\theta}} \right)^{\prime} $$

$$ \boldsymbol{V}_{\mathrm{total}} = \boldsymbol{V}_{\mathrm{within}} + \boldsymbol{V}_{\mathrm{between}} + M^{-1} \boldsymbol{V}_{\mathrm{between}} . $$

An alternative total variance was introduced by Li, Raghunathan, and Rubin (1991) and is given by $$ \tilde{\boldsymbol{V}}_{\mathrm{total}} = \left( 1 + \operatorname{ARIV} \right) \boldsymbol{V}_{\mathrm{within}} $$ where \(\operatorname{ARIV}\) is given by $$ \operatorname{ARIV} = \frac{ \left( 1 + M^{-1} \right) \operatorname{tr} \left( \boldsymbol{V}_{\mathrm{between}} \boldsymbol{V}_{\mathrm{within}}^{-1} \right) }{ k } . $$

References

Li, K. H., Raghunathan, T. E., & Rubin, D. B. (1991). Large-sample significance levels from multiply imputed data using moment-based statistics and an F reference distribution. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 86 (416), 1065–1073. doi:10.1080/01621459.1991.10475152

Rubin, D. B. (1987). Multiple imputation for nonresponse in surveys. John Wiley & Sons, Inc. doi:10.1002/9780470316696

See also

Other Multiple Imputation Helper Functions: MI2List(), MIFit()

Author

Ivan Jacob Agaloos Pesigan

Examples

fit <- lm(Temp ~ ., data = airquality)
set.seed(42)
mifit <- MIFit(
  x = airquality,
  fit = fit,
  fun = "mice",
  M = 3
)
MICombine(mifit)
